SKU — type it or scan it (barcode icon in the field). If this SKU was calculated before, “Already in history” appears under the field — open it and duplicate.

Box: length, width, height — in metres like on the form or in centimetres; the app understands both. Length is always the longest side. Box weight — down to the gram. Pieces per box — 1 if empty.

One piece is optional. If filled in, the form shows a “Piece” column; if not, there is no column and the calculation does not change.

Everything is calculated as you type — there is no “Calculate” button.

All three tiles work the same way: tap — a window with a field showing the current value; type another one and tap “Done”. “Standard” puts the standard value back.
Height includes the pallet itself (15 cm). Standard 1.80 m.
Weight — maximum weight including goods. Standard 700 kg. A switch adds the pallet’s own weight (off by default); the tile then says “+ pallet”.
Overhang — how far boxes may stick out past the pallet edge, per side. Standard is none (most warehouses and carriers accept this), up to 5 cm allowed. Auto layout uses overhang only if more boxes fit.
ADR (hazardous goods) — height 1.20 m only.
All these values are remembered. A tile that differs from the standard is brighter.

The 1.20 × 0.80 pallet from above, boxes in true proportions.

“Auto” looks for the layout with the most boxes: simple rows, rows in different directions and the “pinwheel” (blocks around the centre). If there are several best layouts, “Auto” again shows the next one.

Own layout: drag a box with your finger — it snaps to the pallet edges and neighbouring boxes. Rotate — twist with two fingers (every ~90° turns it) or double tap. Tap — select; “Rotate” and “Remove” act on the selected box. “Add” puts a box in the first free spot.

In the “⋯” menu: “Fill free space” — lay out the first row the way you like and the rest is filled in.

A red box overlaps another or sticks out more than allowed; while there are red boxes you cannot save. The layout in the picture is exactly what gets counted.

Position: if the box has no ↑↑ arrows, the app tries laying it on its side or standing it up and picks whatever fits the most on the pallet (the form height is as the box stands). The “↕ 0.30 m” buttons above the pallet — choose the position yourself (labelled with the height the box stands at). If there are arrows, switch on “Arrows ↑↑ on the box”.

3D — the whole pallet with all layers: drag to turn and tilt (view only).

Layers: “All layers the same” (default) — lay out the first layer, all are the same. Switch it off for separate “Layer 1” and “Layer 2” (e.g. crosswise), alternating 1, 2, 1, 2…. Layer 2 starts as a mirror of the first (interlocking) and follows its changes until you edit it. Under Layer 2 the first layer is shown dashed. A second-layer box must stand on first-layer boxes: centre within the supports (a bridge between two boxes is fine), at least a quarter supported; otherwise red, it would fall. The first layer stands on the pallet.

“All boxes one way” (off by default): on — the layer faces one way only, “Rotate” turns the whole layer. Off — directions may be mixed (a spare box goes to the tray), and an asymmetric layer is mirrored by the next one (interlocking) unless you switched on “All layers the same”.

Tray under the pallet: drag a box that is in the way there — it is set aside; tap the tray to bring it back to a free spot. In 3D the selected layer (1 or 2) is highlighted.

The form looks like the paper card so it is easy to copy. The date is filled in automatically.

Columns: Piece (if entered), Carton, Pallet. Pallet: height including the pallet, number of boxes, goods weight (plus the pallet if added).

Per layer — pieces and boxes in a layer; layers on the pallet.

Flags are set automatically: oversize (piece over 50×30 cm — longer side over 50 and the other over 30), awkward (over 1.2 m), two men lift (box over 35 kg), estimated structure (weight does not allow even one layer).

“Save to history” keeps everything: what you entered, the limits, the layout itself and the result.

Tap a card to open it in full. “Duplicate” copies everything into a new calculation: change what you need (the weight, say) and save a new card — the old one stays.

Long press — menu (open, duplicate, share, delete). Swipe left — delete, with “Undo”.

Search by SKU; you can scan it.
Estimated structure (not even one full layer)
